Definition: of uncertain affinity; Lysias, a Roman:--Lysias.
BiblicalUsage: Lysias, whose full name was Claudius Lysias, was the chief captain in Jerusalem who rescued Paul from the mob and wrote to Governor Felix on his behalf. Felix deferred Paul's case, saying he would decide it when Lysias the chief captain came down, and the letter shows a Roman officer caught between a riot and the law.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Lysias shows how God can use even an unbelieving officer to protect His servant, and the law became a shield for the gospel that day.
RelatedEvents: Paul Before Felix, Festus, and Agrippa
